title: Bangerlore — hosting tech parties we'd want to be attendees at
description: Invite-only house party, Bangalore, since early 2024. ~250 people, every one vetted. 4PM to 4AM.

announcement.text: Thank you for coming to Bangerlore v5!

tweets.name: Aditi Rao
tweets.text: best party in bangalore. not close.

tweets.name: Karan Mehta
tweets.text: Flew in from Bombay for Bangerlore v4. Worth every rupee. Met three people I'm now building with, one of whom wired an angel cheque before the night ended.

tweets.name: Priya S
tweets.text: bangerlore >>> every conference i've been to this year

tweets.name: Rohan Iyer
tweets.text:
Genuinely the only event in the city where I didn't get pitched once and still left with five new friends. That's the vetting working.

Also 4AM. On a Saturday. With that crowd. How.

tweets.name: Neha Kulkarni
tweets.text: 12 hours. 250 people. zero bad conversations. who does that

tweets.name: Sana Qureshi
tweets.text: the no-show ban is the most based policy in indian tech

tweets.name: Dev Sharma
tweets.text: Have been to house parties in SF, London and Berlin that try to do this. None of them get the density right. Bangerlore does. The 80/15/5 mix is the secret and I hope they never change it.

tweets.name: Shreya Menon
tweets.text: If you're a founder, researcher or engineer in India and you haven't been to a Bangerlore yet, fix that. It has quietly become the room where things happen.
